title.narrative: Deutscher Beitrag zur Wiederauffüllung des Asiatischen Entwicklungsfonds (AsDF 14)
German Contribution to the Replenishment of the Asian Development Fund (AsDF 13)

description.narrative: ADF 14 supports this agenda through continued focus on the poorest and most vulnerable DMCs while further emphasizing the need to take bold climate action, deepen regional cooperation and integration (RCI), and address regional public goods (RPGs). ADF 14 will also seek to systematically explore the opportunities to increase collaboration with relevant MDBs. ADB?s concessional assistance DMCs?29 countries with access to ADF grants and concessional ordinary capital resources lending (COL)?continue to face significant development challenges. These include (i) remaining poverty and inequality, (ii) structural vulnerabilities heightened by climate change and disaster risks, (iii) underinvestment in RPGs, (iv) persistent gender gaps, (v) limited private sector development, (vi) deficits in quality infrastructure, (vii) debt vulnerabilities, (viii) and chronic capacity constraints. Grant assistance continues to play a critical role in the support provided by ADB to its DMCs, including to (i) help the poorest and most vulnerable countries, which do not have the capacity to service external loans even on concessional terms, and particularly countries classified as fragile and conflict-affected situations (FCAS) and small island developing states (SIDS), (ii) support DMCs in pursuing thematic priorities, including climate action, RCI and RPGs, and achieving the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 5 transformative gender agenda, (iii) leverage essential and urgent support for DMCs in crisis, and (iv) contribute to knowledge transfer and capacity development.

Große Wirtschafts-, Gesundheits- und Sicherheitsschocks sowie die Folgen des Klimawandels wirken sich negativ auf die Entwicklungsperspektiven der Region aus. ADF Länder (Developing Member Countries (DMCs) stehen dabei insbesondere vor den folgenden Entwicklungsherausforderungen: (i) verbleibende Armut und Ungleichheit, (ii) strukturelle Vulnerabilitäten, die durch den Klimawandel und Katastrophenrisiken verstärkt werden, (iii) Unterinvestitionen in regionale/globale öffentliche Güter (GPG/RPGs), (iv) anhaltende geschlechtsspezifische Unterschiede, (v) begrenzte Entwicklung des privaten Sektors, (vi) Defizite in der Qualitätsinfrastruktur, (vii) Verschuldung sowie (viii) chronische Kapazitätsbeschränkungen.
